fact_rationales.F12: A single S2 and systolic ejection murmur are more typical of Tetralogy of Fallot, but can also be seen in other right heart obstructive lesions.
fact_rationales.F15: An enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature can be seen in several right heart obstructive lesions, but is less specific for Ebstein Anomaly.

fact_rationales.F12: Single S2 and systolic ejection murmur are more typical of ventricular septal defects, but can also be seen in other septal defects.
fact_rationales.F15: Enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is highly suggestive of a left-to-right shunt, which is most consistent with a ventricular septal defect.

fact_rationales.F12: Single S2 and systolic ejection murmur are more typical of truncus arteriosus due to the common arterial trunk, but can be seen in other anomalies as well.
fact_rationales.F15: Enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is indicative of increased blood flow to the lungs, consistent with total anomalous pulmonary venous connection and truncus arteriosus, but less typical for transposition of the great arteries and Ebstein anomaly.

fact_rationales.F11: Nasal flaring, costosternal retractions, and perioral cyanosis are signs of respiratory distress, which can be seen in several cardiac anomalies, but are more typical of total anomalous pulmonary venous connection and truncus arteriosus
fact_rationales.F12: Single S2 and systolic ejection murmur are more typical of truncus arteriosus
fact_rationales.F15: Enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is consistent with total anomalous pulmonary venous connection and truncus arteriosus
fact_rationales.F9: Tachycardia is a non-specific finding, but more commonly associated with truncus arteriosus and transposition of the great arteries

fact_rationales.F12: Single S2 and systolic ejection murmur are more typical of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome due to the underdeveloped left heart structures.
fact_rationales.F15: Enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is highly suggestive of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome, which often presents with increased pulmonary blood flow and cardiomegaly.

fact_rationales.F12: Cardiac auscultation findings are more typical of cardiac causes, making non-cardiac causes less likely.
fact_rationales.F15: Chest imaging findings of an enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature are more suggestive of cardiac causes, making non-cardiac causes less likely, especially respiratory infection.

why.B2.1: Ventricular Septal Defect is a possible diagnosis due to the single S2 and systolic ejection murmur, which can be seen in this condition, and the enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is consistent with a left-to-right shunt.
why.B3.4: Tetralogy of Fallot is a less likely diagnosis due to the presence of increased pulmonary vasculature, which is not typical for this condition.
why.B4.2: Truncus Arteriosus is a possible diagnosis due to the single S2 and systolic ejection murmur, which can be seen in this condition, but the enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is less specific for this diagnosis.
why.B5.2: Metabolic Disorder is the least likely diagnosis due to the cardiac auscultation and chest imaging findings, which are more suggestive of a cardiac cause.
